```{r setup}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

library(PKNCA)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("HourcadePotelleret_2014_trastuzumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("HourcadePotelleret_2014_trastuzumab"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1038/psp.2013.63>

Hourcade-Potelleret et al. (2014) fitted a population PK model to single-dose
intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) trastuzumab data from the phase I/Ib
trial BP22023 and used it to choose the fixed 600 mg SC dose, given every
three weeks (Q3W) without a loading dose, that was later tested in the phase
III HannaH study. The SC formulation contains recombinant human hyaluronidase
(rHuPH20).

The final model has two compartments, first-order SC absorption with
bioavailability F1, and parallel linear and Michaelis-Menten elimination from
the central compartment:

\[
\frac{d\,depot}{dt} = -k_a\,depot,
\qquad
\frac{d\,central}{dt} = k_a\,depot - \frac{CL}{V_2}\,central
  - \frac{V_m\,C_c}{K_m + C_c} - \frac{Q}{V_2}\,central + \frac{Q}{V_3}\,peripheral_1,
\]

with \(C_c = central / V_2\), \(CL = 0.187\,(WT/68)^{0.591}\) L/day and
\(V_2 = 3.43\,(WT/68)^{0.48}\) L. Both weight exponents were held at the
values of the earlier IV trastuzumab model.

# Population

The model was fitted to 786 serum concentrations from 66 individuals who
received 70 single doses: 24 healthy male volunteers (6 mg/kg IV, or 6, 8 or
10 mg/kg SC; 6 per group) and 42 women previously treated for HER2-positive
early breast cancer (6 mg/kg IV, n = 6; 8 or 12 mg/kg SC, n = 20 each; four
women received both 6 mg/kg IV and 8 mg/kg SC). Demographics are not tabulated
in this paper; they were reported with the phase I/Ib trial (Wynne et al., J
Clin Pharmacol 2013;53:192-201). Results "Pharmacokinetic data set" and
Methods "Pharmacokinetic data sets".

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population-meta}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("HourcadePotelleret_2014_trastuzumab"))$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/HourcadePotelleret_2014_trastuzumab.R`. The
supplementary NONMEM output (control stream and final estimates) gives the
same numbers as Table 1 at higher precision, and the OMEGA and SIGMA variances
directly.

| Element | Value | Source location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structure: 2 compartments, first-order absorption, linear + Michaelis-Menten elimination | ODEs above | Results "PopPK modeling"; supplementary control stream `$DES` |
| `lcl` | log(0.187 L/day) | Table 1; NONMEM TH1 |
| `lvc` | log(3.43 L) | Table 1; NONMEM TH2 |
| `lq` | log(0.24 L/day) | Table 1; NONMEM TH3 |
| `lvp` | log(1.71 L) | Table 1; NONMEM TH4 |
| `lfdepot` | log(0.873) | Table 1; NONMEM TH5 |
| `lka` | log(0.28 /day) | Table 1; NONMEM TH6 |
| `lvmax` | log(3.49 mg/day) | Table 1; NONMEM TH9 |
| `lkm` | log(6.12 mg/L) | Table 1; NONMEM TH10 = 6120 ug/L |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.591, held constant | Table 1 ('Fix'); control stream `(WT/68)**THETA(7)` |
| `e_wt_vc` | 0.48, held constant | Table 1 ('Fix'); control stream `(WT/68)**THETA(8)` |
| `etalcl` | 0.0512 | NONMEM OMEGA(1,1); Table 1 22.6% |
| `etalvc` | 0.0449 | NONMEM OMEGA(2,2); Table 1 21.2% |
| `etalfdepot` | 0.0285 | NONMEM OMEGA(4,4); Table 1 16.9% |
| `etalka` | 0.149 | NONMEM OMEGA(5,5); Table 1 38.6% |
| `propSd` | 0.2667 | NONMEM SIGMA(1,1) = 0.0711, square root; Table 1 0.26 |
| Bioavailability on the SC depot only | `f(depot)` | Control stream `F1 = THETA(5)*EXP(ETA(4))` (compartment 1) |
| Reference weight 68 kg | `WT / 68` | Control stream `CLWT`, `V2WT` definitions |

Two quantities quoted in the Results follow directly from these values and
are checked here: the absorption half-life of 2.5 days is
\(\ln 2 / 0.28\), and the statement that the nonlinear pathway is saturated
above about 50 mg/L reflects \(K_m = 6.12\) mg/L.

```{r derived-checks}
c(
  absorption_half_life_day = log(2) / 0.28,
  mm_fraction_of_vmax_at_50_mg_L = 50 / (6.12 + 50)
)
stopifnot(abs(log(2) / 0.28 - 2.5) < 0.05)
```

# Covariate column naming

| Source column | Canonical column | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WT` | `WT` (kg) | Body weight; reference 68 kg. |

# Single-dose profiles (phase I/Ib design)

Figure 1 and Figure 2 of the paper show single-dose profiles after 6 mg/kg IV
and 6 to 12 mg/kg SC. The typical-value profiles below use a 68 kg subject.
The IV infusion duration in BP22023 is not stated in this paper; 90 minutes
(the labelled first-dose infusion time) is assumed.

```{r single-dose-typical, fig.cap = "Typical-value trastuzumab profiles after a single 6 mg/kg IV dose or 6, 8, 10 or 12 mg/kg SC (68 kg subject). Compare with Figure 1 of Hourcade-Potelleret 2014."}
mod <- readModelDb("HourcadePotelleret_2014_trastuzumab")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

wt_ref <- 68
single_obs <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.0625, 0.25, 0.5, seq(1, 150, by = 1))))
single_regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,         ~mg_per_kg, ~cmt,      ~dur,
  "IV 6 mg/kg",       6,          "central", 1.5 / 24,
  "SC 6 mg/kg",       6,          "depot",   0,
  "SC 8 mg/kg",       8,          "depot",   0,
  "SC 10 mg/kg",      10,         "depot",   0,
  "SC 12 mg/kg",      12,         "depot",   0
)

make_single <- function(i, wt) {
  r <- single_regimens[i, ]
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = r$mg_per_kg * wt, dur = r$dur,
               cmt = r$cmt, evid = 1L),
    data.frame(id = i, time = single_obs, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_,
               cmt = "central", evid = 0L)
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(WT = wt, treatment = r$treatment)
}

ev_single <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(single_regimens)), make_single, wt = wt_ref))

# zeroRe() removes the random effects on purpose; rxode2 warns on every
# multi-subject solve without omega, so muffle that one warning only.
sim_single <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_single,
                  keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  }
)

ggplot(sim_single |> dplyr::filter(time > 0),
       aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Trastuzumab Cc (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical-value single-dose profiles") +
  theme_bw()
```

The dose-normalised SC profiles converge at high concentrations and separate
in the terminal phase, where the Michaelis-Menten pathway is no longer
saturated (Figure 1b of the paper).

```{r single-dose-dn, fig.cap = "Dose-normalised typical-value SC profiles. Compare with Figure 1b of Hourcade-Potelleret 2014."}
sim_single |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, grepl("^SC", treatment)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dose_mg_per_kg = as.numeric(sub("SC ([0-9]+) mg/kg", "\\1", treatment)),
    Cc_dn = Cc / dose_mg_per_kg
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc_dn, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Cc per mg/kg dose (mg/L per mg/kg)",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Visual predictive check

A stochastic simulation of 100 subjects per arm for the 6 mg/kg IV and
8 mg/kg SC arms, with residual error, mirrors the structure of Figure 2.
Body weight is drawn from the paper's virtual-population distribution
(mean 68 kg, SD 11 kg) because the phase I/Ib weights are not given here.

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles (with residual error) after a single 6 mg/kg IV or 8 mg/kg SC dose. Compare with Figure 2 of Hourcade-Potelleret 2014."}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20140102)
n_vpc <- 100
vpc_obs <- c(0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 7, 9, 14, 21, 34, 42, 84, 150)
make_vpc_arm <- function(arm, id_offset) {
  wt <- pmax(stats::rnorm(n_vpc, 68, 11), 40)
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_vpc)
  is_iv <- arm == "IV 6 mg/kg"
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = ids, time = 0,
               amt = if (is_iv) 6 * wt else 8 * wt,
               dur = if (is_iv) 1.5 / 24 else 0,
               cmt = if (is_iv) "central" else "depot", evid = 1L, WT = wt),
    data.frame(id = rep(ids, each = length(vpc_obs)),
               time = rep(vpc_obs, n_vpc), amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_,
               cmt = "central", evid = 0L, WT = rep(wt, each = length(vpc_obs)))
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = arm)
}
set.seed(20140102)
ev_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_vpc_arm("IV 6 mg/kg", 0L),
  make_vpc_arm("SC 8 mg/kg", n_vpc)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_vpc, keep = "treatment",
                           returnType = "data.frame")

sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(sim)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), q50 = median(sim), q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue4", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Trastuzumab concentration (mg/L)",
       caption = "Line: median; band: 5th-95th percentile of simulated observations.") +
  theme_bw()
```

## PKNCA: single-dose exposure and bioavailability

The paper states that 6 mg/kg IV and SC data in healthy volunteers suggested
a bioavailability above 80%. With the nonlinear elimination pathway the SC/IV
AUC ratio is not exactly F1 = 0.873: the slower-rising SC profile spends more
time at concentrations where the Michaelis-Menten pathway is not saturated, so
the typical-value ratio comes out a little lower (about 0.81).

```{r pknca-single}
conc_single <- sim_single |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_single <- ev_single |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

nca_single <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_single, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                   concu = "mg/L", timeu = "day"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_single, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                         aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))

nca_single_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_single$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_single_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (day)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (mg*day/L)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (day)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = "Typical-value single-dose NCA (68 kg subject).")

auc_iv6 <- nca_single_tbl$aucinf.obs[nca_single_tbl$treatment == "IV 6 mg/kg"]
auc_sc6 <- nca_single_tbl$aucinf.obs[nca_single_tbl$treatment == "SC 6 mg/kg"]
f_apparent <- auc_sc6 / auc_iv6
f_apparent
# Deterministic (typical-value) quantity: the ratio departs from F1 only
# through the Michaelis-Menten pathway, which removes a slightly larger share
# of the slower-rising SC dose.
stopifnot(f_apparent > 0.80, f_apparent < 0.90)
```

# Dose selection: fixed SC dose versus weight-based IV (Table 2, Figure 3)

The paper simulated the reference IV regimen (8 mg/kg loading dose, then
6 mg/kg Q3W) and fixed SC doses of 400, 500, 600 and 700 mg Q3W without a
loading dose, in virtual patients with body weight mean 68 kg and SD 11 kg
(130 per arm, 100 replicates). Here one replicate of 150 patients per arm is
simulated over eight cycles. The IV loading dose is infused over 90 minutes
and maintenance doses over 30 minutes, as in the label.

```{r dose-selection-events}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2014)
set.seed(2014)
n_arm <- 150
arms <- c("IV 8/6 mg/kg", "SC 400 mg", "SC 500 mg", "SC 600 mg", "SC 700 mg")
dose_times <- seq(0, 147, by = 21)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  0:147,
  as.vector(outer(dose_times, c(0.0208, 0.0625, 0.25, 0.5), "+"))
)))

make_arm <- function(a) {
  ids <- (a - 1L) * n_arm + seq_len(n_arm)
  wt <- pmax(stats::rnorm(n_arm, 68, 11), 35)
  doses <- data.frame(
    id = rep(ids, each = length(dose_times)),
    time = rep(dose_times, n_arm),
    WT = rep(wt, each = length(dose_times)),
    evid = 1L
  )
  if (a == 1L) {
    doses <- doses |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        amt = ifelse(time == 0, 8, 6) * WT,
        dur = ifelse(time == 0, 1.5, 0.5) / 24,
        cmt = "central"
      )
  } else {
    doses <- doses |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = c(400, 500, 600, 700)[a - 1L], dur = 0, cmt = "depot")
  }
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = rep(ids, each = length(obs_times)),
    time = rep(obs_times, n_arm),
    WT = rep(wt, each = length(obs_times)),
    evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_, cmt = "central"
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = arms[a])
}

ev_ds <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(arms), make_arm)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, evid)

sim_ds <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_ds, keep = c("treatment", "WT"),
                          returnType = "data.frame")
```

The observation at each dose time is solved before that dose is given, so the
day-21 and day-147 values are the Cycle 1 and predose Cycle 8 troughs.

```{r trough-check}
iv1 <- sim_ds |> dplyr::filter(id == 1, time %in% c(21, 21.0208))
iv1[, c("time", "Cc")]
stopifnot(iv1$Cc[iv1$time == 21] < iv1$Cc[iv1$time == 21.0208] / 2)
```

## PKNCA by treatment and cycle

AUC0-21 days and Cmax come from PKNCA for Cycle 1 (days 0-21) and Cycle 7
(days 126-147). Ctrough is the concentration at the end of each interval
(day 21, and day 147 = predose Cycle 8). It is read directly off the solved
profile and carried under the PKNCA code `ctrough`, because PKNCA 0.12.1
returns `NA` for `ctrough` on an interval that does not start at time 0.

```{r pknca-ds}
conc_ds <- sim_ds |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment, WT)
dose_ds <- ev_ds |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals_ds <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 126), end = c(21, 147),
  auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE
)

nca_ds <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_ds, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                   concu = "mg/L", timeu = "day"),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ds, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
  intervals = intervals_ds
))

trough_ds <- conc_ds |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(21, 147)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    id, treatment,
    cycle = ifelse(time == 21, "Cycle 1", "Cycle 7"),
    PPTESTCD = "ctrough", PPORRES = Cc
  )
stopifnot(nrow(trough_ds) == 2 * n_arm * length(arms))

nca_ds_res <- as.data.frame(nca_ds$result) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cycle = ifelse(start == 0, "Cycle 1", "Cycle 7")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, cycle, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(trough_ds)
stopifnot(!anyNA(nca_ds_res$PPORRES))

nca_ds_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("ctrough", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, cycle, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05), median = median(PPORRES),
    q95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Cycle" = cycle, "Parameter" = PPTESTCD,
                "5th percentile" = q05, "Median" = median,
                "95th percentile" = q95) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1,
               caption = "Simulated Ctrough (mg/L) and AUC0-21 days (mg*day/L) by regimen and cycle.")
```

## Comparison with Table 2

Table 2 of the paper gives the median, over 100 replicates, of the
per-replicate 5th percentile, median and 95th percentile for the IV reference
and the 600 mg SC regimen. The simulated medians are compared below.

```{r comparison-table2}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,     ~cycle,    ~ctrough, ~auclast,
  "IV 8/6 mg/kg", "Cycle 1", 34,       1349,
  "SC 600 mg",    "Cycle 1", 39,       1241,
  "IV 8/6 mg/kg", "Cycle 7", 46,       1796,
  "SC 600 mg",    "Cycle 7", 79,       2408
)

simulated_long <- nca_ds_res |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment %in% published$treatment,
                PPTESTCD %in% c("ctrough", "auclast"))

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated_long,
  reference = published,
  by = c("treatment", "cycle"),
  units = c(ctrough = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*day/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

cmp |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Cycle" = cycle) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated medians versus Hourcade-Potelleret 2014 Table 2 medians.",
      "* differs from the published median by more than 20%."
    )
  )

pct_check <- simulated_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, cycle, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(published, c(ctrough, auclast),
                        names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("treatment", "cycle", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - ref) / ref)
pct_diff <- pct_check$pct_diff
stopifnot(
  length(pct_diff) == 8,
  # A mis-transcribed clearance, volume, bioavailability or unit moves these
  # medians by tens of percent; the median of 150 subjects moves a few
  # percent between cohorts.
  median(abs(pct_diff)) < 10,
  all(abs(pct_diff) < 25)
)
```

Seven of the eight medians agree within 5%. The exception is the IV Cycle 1
AUC0-21 days, about 15% above the paper's 1,349 mg\*day/L, while the IV
Cycle 1 trough and the IV Cycle 7 AUC agree within 4%. The paper does not
describe how its Cycle 1 AUC was computed (sampling grid or infusion
handling), and no parameter in Table 1 can raise the Cycle 1 AUC without also
moving the trough, so the difference is recorded rather than adjusted.

The paper's percentile ranges for the predose Cycle 8 trough (IV 23-84 mg/L,
SC 38-143 mg/L) are reproduced closely. Its Cycle 1 ranges (IV 27-40 mg/L,
SC 35-46 mg/L) are narrower than the simulated ones; the reason is not
stated. With 22.6% IIV on CL, 21.2% on V2, 16.9% on F1 and 38.6% on Ka, a
Cycle 1 trough coefficient of variation of roughly 25-30% is expected, and the
observed HannaH Cycle 1 SC troughs (5th-95th percentile 12-66 mg/L) were wider
still.

## Dose-selection criterion (Figure 3)

600 mg was the lowest SC dose whose Cycle 1 and predose Cycle 8 troughs were
at least as high as with the IV reference.

```{r figure-3, fig.cap = "Simulated Ctrough at Cycle 1 and predose Cycle 8, and AUC0-21 days at Cycle 1, by regimen. Compare with Figure 3 of Hourcade-Potelleret 2014."}
fig3 <- nca_ds_res |>
  dplyr::filter(
    (PPTESTCD == "ctrough") |
      (PPTESTCD == "auclast" & cycle == "Cycle 1")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    panel = dplyr::case_when(
      PPTESTCD == "ctrough" & cycle == "Cycle 1" ~ "Ctrough Cycle 1 (mg/L)",
      PPTESTCD == "ctrough" ~ "Ctrough predose Cycle 8 (mg/L)",
      TRUE ~ "AUC0-21 days Cycle 1 (mg*day/L)"
    ),
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = arms)
  )

ggplot(fig3, aes(treatment, PPORRES)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.6) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, fill = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

trough_med <- nca_ds_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "ctrough") |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, cycle) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cycle, values_from = median)
trough_med

med <- function(trt, cyc) trough_med[[cyc]][trough_med$treatment == trt]
# The SC 500 and 600 mg Cycle 1 medians sit about 15% either side of the IV
# median, several times the cohort-to-cohort noise of a 150-subject median.
stopifnot(
  med("SC 600 mg", "Cycle 1") > med("IV 8/6 mg/kg", "Cycle 1"),
  med("SC 600 mg", "Cycle 7") > med("IV 8/6 mg/kg", "Cycle 7"),
  med("SC 500 mg", "Cycle 1") < med("IV 8/6 mg/kg", "Cycle 1")
)
```

## Heavier patients (> 75 kg)

The paper reports, for virtual patients above 75 kg, median (5th-95th
percentile) Cycle 1 troughs of 36 (33-39) mg/L SC and 38 (34-44) mg/L IV,
and predose Cycle 8 troughs of 69 (33-130) mg/L SC and 53 (25-99) mg/L IV.
The subgroup here is roughly a quarter of each 150-patient arm, so its
medians are noisier than the full-arm values.

```{r heavy}
nca_ds_res |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "ctrough",
                treatment %in% c("IV 8/6 mg/kg", "SC 600 mg")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::distinct(conc_ds, id, WT), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::filter(WT > 75) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, cycle) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(), q05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
    median = median(PPORRES), q95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "Cycle" = cycle,
                "5th percentile" = q05, "Median" = median,
                "95th percentile" = q95) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1,
               caption = "Simulated Ctrough (mg/L) in patients above 75 kg.")
```

## Retrospective comparison with HannaH (Figure 4)

The paper compared the dose-selection simulations with observed HannaH data
(Results "Retrospective validation of the pharmacokinetic model"); these
observed values are quoted for context and are not used in any check.

| Quantity | Regimen | Paper simulation, median (5th-95th) | HannaH observed, median (5th-95th) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ctrough Cycle 1 (mg/L) | SC 600 mg | 39 (35-46) | 29 (12-66) |
| Ctrough predose Cycle 8 (mg/L) | IV 8/6 mg/kg | 46 (23-84) | 49 (23-106) |
| Ctrough predose Cycle 8 (mg/L) | SC 600 mg | 79 (38-143) | 70 (23-150) |
| AUC0-21 days Cycle 7 (mg*day/L) | IV 8/6 mg/kg | 1,796 (1,202-2,605) | 1,970 (1,320-3,310) |
| AUC0-21 days Cycle 7 (mg*day/L) | SC 600 mg | 2,408 (1,464-4,007) | 2,260 (1,090-4,010) |

```{r figure-4, fig.cap = "Simulated concentration-time profiles (median and 5th-95th percentile, no residual error) for the IV reference and 600 mg SC regimens over eight cycles. Compare with Figure 4e,f of Hourcade-Potelleret 2014."}
sim_ds |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment %in% c("IV 8/6 mg/kg", "SC 600 mg"), time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q50 = median(Cc),
                   q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +

  theme_bw()
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error.** Table 1 prints the proportional residual error as 0.26.
  The supplementary NONMEM output gives SIGMA = 0.0711, whose square root is
  0.2667; the more precise value is used.
* **Fixed-zero random effects omitted.** The control stream declares etas on
  V3, Vmax and Km with variances fixed to zero; they have no effect and are
  not carried into the model.
* **Bioavailability random effect.** As in the control stream, F1 is
  log-normal (`F1 = 0.873 * exp(eta)`), so a small fraction of simulated
  individuals have F1 above 1.
* **Units.** The control stream scales concentrations to ug/L
  (`S2 = V2/1000`, Km = 6120 ug/L). The packaged model works in mg and L, so
  concentrations are mg/L and Km is 6.12 mg/L, as in Table 1.
* **Covariate distribution.** The phase I/Ib demographics are not given in
  this paper. Simulations draw body weight from Normal(68, 11) kg, the
  distribution the paper used for its virtual population, truncated below at
  35 or 40 kg.
* **IV infusion durations.** 90 minutes for the single phase I/Ib dose and
  the 8 mg/kg loading dose, 30 minutes for 6 mg/kg maintenance doses (the
  labelled administration times quoted in the paper's introduction). The
  phase I/Ib infusion time is not stated in this paper.
* **Simulation size.** The paper used 130 patients per arm and 100
  replicates; this vignette uses one replicate of 150 patients per arm.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found on Europe PMC for
  doi:10.1038/psp.2013.63 (checked 2026-11-20).
